2. Due dates for filing of Income Tax Returns and Audit Reports for AY 2026-27 are extended in the cases of persons mentioned at Sl.No.2 in the Table below Explanation2 to Sub-section (1) of Section 139 of Income Tax Act 1961 vide Circular No.07/2026 dated 28th September,2026.
3. Form 1 under the “Foreign Assets of Small Taxpayers Disclosure Scheme” is now available for filing.
4. ITR-1, ITR-2, ITR-3, ITR-4, ITR-5, ITR-6 and ITR-7 for AY 2026-27 are available for filing through both online and offline utilities.

7. Excel utilities for filing Updated return for ITR-1 to 7 for AY 2022-23 as per Finance Act, 2026 are available for filing !

NRI Income Tax Return: A Comprehensive Guide

Non-Resident Indians (NRIs) may be required to file an income tax return in India for income that is taxable in India. Their tax liability depends on residential status, the source and nature of income, applicable deductions, and any relief available under a .

Residential status is determined under the , primarily based on the individual's stay in India during the relevant financial year and, in certain cases, their stay during preceding years and other statutory conditions.
An individual who does not qualify as a resident under the applicable rules is generally treated as a  for Indian income-tax purposes.
NRIs are generally taxed in India on income that is , subject to applicable provisions. Common sources include:
received, accrued, or deemed to be received or accrue in India
Salary for services performed in India is generally taxable in India, subject to applicable rules.
Rent from property in India is taxable. Eligible deductions, including the applicable standard deduction and municipal taxes, may be claimed subject to the law.
Gains from the sale of Indian property, shares, securities, or mutual funds may be taxable. The applicable treatment depends on the asset, holding period, and relevant tax provisions.
Interest from Indian bank accounts and deposits may be taxable. Interest on eligible  is generally exempt subject to applicable conditions, while NRO interest is generally taxable.
Business income, professional income, dividends, and other India-linked income may also be taxable.
NRIs are generally subject to the income-tax rates applicable to individuals, but the applicable regime, slab rates, special rates, surcharge, cess, and other provisions depend on the .
relevant financial year and nature of income

Special tax rates may apply to certain types of income, such as specified capital gains. Surcharge and health & education cess may also apply where applicable.
Depending on the income and applicable tax regime, NRIs may be eligible for certain deductions and tax benefits, including:
Eligible investments and payments such as life insurance premiums, EPF contributions, and eligible home-loan principal repayment.
Eligible health insurance premiums, subject to applicable conditions.
NRIs may claim relief under an applicable Double Taxation Avoidance Agreement where the same income is taxable in India and another country, subject to the treaty and prescribed conditions.
Certain deductions, exemptions, and allowances may be available depending on the nature of income and the applicable tax regime.

NRIs should determine their residential status and taxable Indian income before selecting the appropriate ITR form. The return should include relevant Indian income, eligible deductions, taxes paid or deducted at source, and applicable foreign/treaty information where required.
Timely and accurate filing helps NRIs maintain tax compliance, claim eligible refunds, and manage their Indian tax obligations effectively.
